blocks.title: The phone, in detail.
blocks.lead: Gestures, the lock screen, notifications and settings on Etesian for LineageOS 24. Published builds exist for the F(x)tec Pro1-X only.

paragraphs: The latest published ROM is version {{rom.version}} ({{rom.date}}). Work built since then is marked “not in a release yet” until a newer release is published.

items.title: Swipe in from the left or right edge
items.text: Leaves the app: it keeps running and waits in Open applications. Each side can be set to go to a different home view {{rom.pending:2026-11-15}}.

items.title: Swipe up from the bottom edge
items.text: A plain swipe leaves the app, as from the sides. Hold still for about half a second on the way up and the first row of Applications comes up; the app drops onto it and stays until you tap an icon or the app.

blocks.heading: Etesian in a container
paragraphs: The same Etesian, built on LineageOS 24 for x86_64, runs as a Docker image the way Redroid does: one container, no virtual machine, on a Linux host. Reach it with adb and scrcpy. It is built with the release keys and boot-tested in a throwaway virtual machine before each release; the image and how to run it are on the Download page.

home.title: A calm, gesture-first phone.
home.lead: No home button, no navigation bar. Swipe in from an edge to leave an app, see everything new in one list, and let your content fill the screen. Etesian is built on LineageOS 24; published builds exist for the F(x)tec Pro1-X only. Version {{rom.version}}.

home.heading: Swipe, don’t press
home.intro: The edges of the screen do the work, the same way in every app.

items.title: Swipe in from the left or right edge
items.text: Leaves the app. It keeps running and waits in Open applications.

items.title: Swipe down from the top edge
items.text: Closes the app: the N9 swipe-down close.

items.title: Swipe up from the bottom edge
items.text: Leaves the app; hold on the way up and the first row of Applications comes up.

items.title: Swipe sideways on the lock screen
items.text: Unlocks. There is no unlock button.

items.title: Tap the status bar
items.text: Opens the status menu: profile, volume, connectivity and battery.

items.title: Pinch in Open applications
items.text: Zooms between a carousel and 2, 3 or 4 cards per row.

home.heading: Home views
home.intro: Home is three views side by side, plus optional Widgets and News views. Swipe between them.

items.title: Events
items.text: Notifications, today’s calendar and your feeds in one list, with the weather.

items.title: Applications
items.text: Every app as a lit squircle icon, with folders.

items.title: Open applications
items.text: Live cards of the running apps.

items.title: Widgets and News
items.text: Optional views: Belle-style widgets, and Glance’s news (News view {{rom.pending:2026-11-15}}).

home.heading: The lock screen
home.text: A large, thin clock and the full date. Notifications are dark translucent cards at the bottom: the newest in full, the rest stacked beneath them. An optional glance line and the weather can sit under the clock, and emergency information is reachable from the lock screen. Swipe sideways to unlock.

home.heading: Additions, off by default
home.text: Everything the N9 did not have is optional and starts switched off, so the phone starts as a pure N9 experience. Each addition sits in Settings on the page of what it changes, most with a live preview of that part of the phone at the top. Try the Lock screen page here. N9-style replacements keep every option of the stock Android screens they replace.

home.heading: Settings where you expect them
home.intro: Pages that change how something looks start with a live preview of it.

items.title: Status menu
items.text: An optional toggle strip and sliders, with an edit mode to add, remove and reorder rows.

items.title: Open applications
items.text: Carousel, split screen and arranging the cards by hand.

items.title: Lock screen
items.text: Notification style, a glance line and the weather under the clock.

items.title: Emergency information
items.text: Medical details and emergency contacts, reachable from the lock screen.

items.title: Sharing
items.text: An N9-style share sheet and sharing a Wi-Fi network as a QR code.

items.title: Toolbar
items.text: The N9 bar under every app, with Back on the left.

home.heading: From the first second
paragraphs: A boot animation and a startup sound made for Etesian, in the spirit of the N9 rather than copied from it, set the tone before the lock screen appears.
